result.topic_en: Euler derives a practical series rule for the height of a vertical fountain jet in terms of the ratio of pipe length to diameter and the elevation of the water in the reservoir, using the empirical friction constant.
result.transcription:
380 TENTAMEN THEORIAE
ſi ergo diameter huius aquae ductus ſit $=d$, erit
$gg=\frac{1}{4}\pi dd$, et $g=\frac{1}{2}d\sqrt{\pi}$. Cum ergo collegerim ex
experimentis eſſe $\alpha=\frac{1}{4540}$, erit $\frac{g}{\alpha}=2270\,d\sqrt{\pi}=4023\,d$.
Calculus ergo ſatis exacte ſe habebit, ſi poſito canalis
diametro $=d$, ſumamus $\frac{g}{\alpha}=4000\,d$.

108. Cum igitur ſit $v=\frac{g}{\alpha b}\left(q-\frac{\alpha bl}{g}\right)\left(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}}\right)$, ob
$1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}}=\frac{\alpha b}{g}-\frac{\alpha^2b^2}{2g^2}+\frac{\alpha^3b^3}{6g^3}-\frac{\alpha^4b^4}{24g^4}-\text{etc.}$
habebitur altitudo iactus verticalis:
$v=\left(q-\frac{\alpha bl}{g}\right)\left(1-\frac{\alpha b}{2g}+\frac{\alpha^2b^2}{6g^2}-\frac{\alpha^3b^3}{24g^3}+\text{etc.}\right)$
vbi eſt $\frac{\alpha b}{g}=\frac{b}{4000d}$.

109. En ergo ſequentem regulam pro altitudine
iactus, in quouis fonte ſaliente inuenienda: Diuidatur
tota canalis longitudo per diametrum amplitudinis eiusdem
canalis, et quotus ponatur $=n$, tum ſit
$N=1-\frac{n}{2\cdot4000}+\frac{n^2}{6\cdot4000^2}-\frac{n^3}{24\cdot4000^3}+\frac{n^4}{120\cdot4000^4}-\text{etc.}$
Tum ſit $q$ eleuatio aquae in caſtello ſupra fontem, eritque
altitudo iactus
$v=Nq-\frac{1}{400}Nn$ pedum.
Vel poſito $\frac{1}{400}Nn=M$, erit altitudo iactus in pedibus
expreſſa $v=Nq-M$.

110. Ex dato ergo numero $n$, qui prodit, ſi longitudo
canalis per eius diametrum diuidatur, colligantur valores
litterarum N et M; tum prior numerus N multiplice-
tur per eleuationem aquae in caſtello ſupra fontem,
quae altitudo in pedibus ſit expreſſa, et ab hoc pro-
ducto
